content.title: About
content.content: Crisp, cherry are crunchy dried cherries processed with a special technique that preserves their natural sweetness and bright flavor. The cherries are dehydrated at low temperature, retaining most of the vitamins, minerals, and the characteristic aroma of ripe cherries.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dried cherries retain up to 80 % of the vitamin C found in fresh fruit.
Traditional folk medicine used dried cherries to aid digestion.
Crisp, cherry contains no added sugar or preservatives.
Cherries belong to the Rosaceae family and are relatives of apples, pears, and peaches.
The crunchy texture is achieved by rapid dehydration at temperatures not exceeding 45 °C.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cherries contain anthocyanins and polyphenols that help combat free radicals and reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Flavonoids in cherries improve vascular function and may lower LDL cholesterol levels.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Carotenoids and vitamin A present in cherries contribute to good vision.

items.title: Cherry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cherries, ranging from skin rashes to more severe symptoms.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although no sugar is added, the natural sugars in cherries may be a concern for people with diabetes.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Cherries have moderate acidity, which can cause discomfort for those sensitive to acidic foods.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Crisp, cherry can be enjoyed as a snack, added to granola, yogurt, baked goods, salads, or used as a sweet note in sauces and desserts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a dry, cool place in an airtight container. For long‑term storage, keep refrigerated to preserve crunch and aroma.
